title: Geometric points of a universal homeomorphism from a stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, stacks in groupoids, and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\mathcal A/S$ be Deligne--Mumford and $Y/S$ an algebraic space. Suppose $q:\mathcal A\to Y$ is a universal homeomorphism. It is a universal homeomorphism when every base change by an algebraic stack induces a homeomorphism on underlying point spaces. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; smooth uses [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The underlying points are field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Then for every algebraically closed field $K$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, $q$ induces a bijection $\pi_0(\mathcal A(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}Y(K)$, where $\pi_0$ means isomorphism classes in the fibre groupoid. The same conclusion holds for every base change $\mathcal A\times_Y Y_1\to Y_1$ by an algebraic space $Y_1\to Y$.

source.place: Tags 0CPN (lemma-universally-injective), 0DTM (lemma-universally-injective-point), and 0CI7 (definition-universal-homeomorphism). Target is an algebraic space, so the induced map on isomorphism classes is bijective.

proof.text: For each algebraic-stack test $\mathcal Z\to Y$, the homeomorphism $|\mathcal A\times_Y\mathcal Z|\to|\mathcal Z|$ is injective. Thus $q$ is universally injective in the point-space sense. Taking the identity test $Y\to Y$ also makes $|q|$ surjective. Composition with $q$ sends isomorphic objects to the same element of $Y(K)$, since an algebraic space is regarded as a discrete groupoid. Hence it defines the asserted map on isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 0CI7 (definition-universal-homeomorphism); pointwise consequences of the definition.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed $K$ and $y\in Y(K)$. Surjectivity of $|q|$ puts $[y]$ in its image. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-universally-injective-point-lift] to $q$ and $y$, using universal injectivity from step 1. This gives $a\in\mathcal A(K)$ and an isomorphism $q(a)\simeq y$. In the discrete groupoid $Y(K)$ this is equality. The class $[a]$ is therefore a preimage of $y$, proving surjectivity over this same field $K$.

If $a,b\in\mathcal A(K)$ have $q(a)=q(b)$, this equality supplies an isomorphism $\beta:q(a)\simeq q(b)$ in $Y(K)$. By the implication (1) to (3) of [lem-sfb-stack-universal-injectivity-criteria], universal injectivity of $q$ gives an isomorphism $\alpha:a\simeq b$ with $q(\alpha)=\beta$. Thus $[a]=[b]$. Together with step 2 this proves the desired bijection. No claim that $\alpha$ is unique is needed.

Let $h:Y_1\to Y$ be any algebraic-space map. By the definition of the 2-fibre product, an object of $(\mathcal A\times_Y Y_1)(K)$ is a triple $(a,z,\gamma)$ with $z\in Y_1(K)$ and $\gamma:q(a)\simeq h(z)$. As $Y(K)$ is discrete, $\gamma$ is the unique arrow witnessing the equality. For any $z$, step 2 supplies $a$ with $q(a)=h(z)$, giving such a triple. Two triples above the same $z$ have isomorphic $a$ components by step 3, and that isomorphism is automatically compatible with their structural arrows: both images in the discrete groupoid $Y(K)$ are the unique arrow between the same objects. It therefore gives an isomorphism of triples. The projection to $z$ is bijective on isomorphism classes, proving the base-change clause without any restriction on $h$.
